questions.question_text:
a) What is one example of renewable energy?
b) What is one example of non-renewable energy?
c) Why are fossil fuels considered non-renewable?
d) What is one advantage of wind energy?

keywords_required: b) Coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear (uranium).
c) They take millions of years to form and cannot be replenished on a human timescale (they will run out).
d) It produces no greenhouse gases, it is free once built, and the resource (wind) is infinite.

questions.question_text: Give two differences between renewable and non-renewable energy sources. [2]

keywords_required: Renewables can be naturally replenished (won't run out), whereas non-renewables are finite and will run out.
Non-renewables (fossil fuels) release carbon dioxide when burned, whereas renewables generally produce zero emissions.

questions.question_text: Why is geothermal energy considered renewable energy? [2]

keywords_required: It uses heat generated continuously from the Earth's core/mantle.
This heat is naturally occurring and inexhaustible, so it will never run out.

questions.question_text: Why can fuelwood be considered either renewable or non-renewable? [2]

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2: Explain dual nature of fuelwood.
keywords_required: It is renewable if trees are replanted at the same rate they are cut down (afforestation).
It becomes non-renewable if deforestation occurs faster than trees can naturally regrow.

questions.question_text: Justify the use of renewable energy sources. [3]

keywords_required: They do not emit greenhouse gases, helping to mitigate climate change.
They improve energy security because a country does not have to rely on importing finite fossil fuels.
The "fuel" (wind, sun) is free and infinite, leading to long-term sustainability.
